title: FairLend Landing Page Hero Synthesis
summary: Eight one-hero landing page concepts that blend FairLend corporate/brokerage trust with a high-converting builder project-review flow.
whenToUse: Use for deciding which landing page hero direction should anchor FairLend's broader company positioning while converting construction build-financing borrowers.
riskGates: Do not make a collage or contact sheet.
Do not invent awards, rates, endorsements, or third-party logos.
Generated typography is directional; final copy should be composited deterministically after a route is selected.

review.title: FairLend hero synthesis concepts
review.summary: Eight unique landing-page hero mockups blending brokerage trust with the high-converting project-review flow.

families.title: Licensed Project Review
families.summary: Lead with the conversion quiz, but flank it with brokerage licensing and corporate proof so the two-minute review feels credible.
families.businessGoal: Increase builder starts without losing the trust created by the brokerage/company page.
families.scene: A polished desktop landing-page hero screenshot for FairLend: warm off-white page, full top navigation, large editorial serif headline on the left, a compact Step 1 of 7 project-review module near the CTA, and a right-side Canadian multiplex construction image with a translucent licensed brokerage proof card.
families.focus: Primary focus is the builder/developer starting a project review, with secondary focus on licensed brokerage legitimacy.
families.decision: Can the homepage become a company-trust hero and a builder conversion entry point at once?
elements: large serif headline about build financing and fair lending
constraints: one unique hero page only, no collage, no multiple thumbnails, no mood board
premium brokerage aesthetic, low-radius UI, clean whitespace
conversion elements must be prominent but not gimmicky
generated text should be sparse and approximate, final text can be rebuilt later
families.avoid: contact sheets, page grids, generic SaaS dashboard, fake awards, fake rates, fake partner marks, discount framing, overly rounded cartoon UI

families.title: Company Trust With Quiz
families.summary: Keep the first page's broad 'Building the future of Fair Lending' posture, then place a slim builder qualification card directly below the promise.
families.businessGoal: Retain corporate credibility while making the next action unmistakable for build-financing prospects.
families.scene: A high-fidelity FairLend homepage hero mockup with a monumental serif company headline on a warm beige canvas, a realistic Canadian urban housing image fading into blue blueprint lines, and a centered embedded review card with progress dots, low-friction chips, and two stacked CTAs.
families.focus: The synthesis of brand narrative and practical builder qualification.
families.decision: Does a corporate homepage hero convert better when the review flow is embedded as the first action?
elements: subcopy about build financing, private mortgages, investor access
transparent terms and technology-led underwriting proof points
constraints: one page hero only
the review card should feel native to the brokerage brand
use generous editorial spacing
avoid dense explanatory text
families.avoid: separate landing pages side by side, collage, fake regulatory seals, heavy gradients, generic tech startup look

families.title: Progress Draw Control Plane
families.summary: Turn the hero into an operational control plane: roadmap, draw grouping, evidence, and funding release all visible in one premium hero.
families.businessGoal: Speak directly to developers who care about draw execution while maintaining FairLend's institutional confidence.
families.scene: A desktop landing-page hero mockup with the FairLend nav, a strong serif headline about financing that moves with construction progress, and a right-side product-like visual showing a construction roadmap, milestone cards, draw group brackets, evidence status, and a small licensed brokerage badge over a tasteful Canadian build site image.
families.focus: Construction draw management clarity, with brokerage authority as the credibility layer.
families.decision: Would developer/operators convert better when the hero visual shows the actual draw workflow instead of only a finished building?
constraints: product UI should be visual and sparse, not a dense dashboard
maintain warm FairLend editorial tone
CTA remains visible above the fold
families.avoid: generic analytics SaaS, fake customer data, tiny unreadable tables, collage, overly dark fintech styling

families.title: Site-Verified Brokerage
families.summary: Use the site-visit/evidence angle as proof: FairLend funds verified progress, not paperwork promises.
families.businessGoal: Convert serious builders by making the reimbursement-draw logic feel concrete and governed.
families.scene: A sophisticated FairLend hero mockup showing a construction site or partially completed multiplex on the right, with overlaid evidence cards, geofence/location verification cue, site-visit note, and a small brokerage/license proof card. The left side carries a serif headline, low-friction chips, Step 1 of 7 progress, and a coral Start project review CTA.
families.decision: Does evidence-first construction language make the financing offer feel more credible and specific?
elements: construction site / partially built multiplex image
constraints: the construction evidence should feel professional, not surveillance-heavy
keep legal/proof cues restrained
do not imply proactive advance funding
families.avoid: collage, police-like geofence visuals, fake personal data, fake loan approvals, aggressive sales design

families.title: Two-Door, Builder First
families.summary: Keep FairLend's two-sided business clear, but make Build Financing the dominant path and Investor Platform the secondary path.
families.businessGoal: Clarify FairLend as brokerage and investment company while optimizing for the builder/developer segment.
families.scene: A premium FairLend desktop hero mockup with one large left headline and two action panels below: a dominant build-financing project-review panel with progress dots and coral CTA, plus a quieter investor-platform panel. On the right, a realistic Canadian multifamily property fades from blueprint sketch to completed structure, with a brokerage license card tucked near the image.
families.focus: Segment clarity without splitting the page into equal competing heroes.
families.decision: Can the hero serve both borrowers and investors while clearly prioritizing the conversion-critical builder flow?
elements: two path panels with build financing dominant
deep green and coral FairLend palette
constraints: do not create a two-page collage
build path must be visually primary
investor path should not steal the main CTA
families.avoid: equal-weight split causing choice paralysis, generic tabs, fake investor returns, cluttered nav

families.title: Capital Confidence Meter
families.summary: Translate working-capital constraints and lender policy into a builder-friendly feasibility readout in the hero.
families.businessGoal: Attract developers who need to know whether their project can survive draw timing, fees, and capital limits.
families.scene: A FairLend landing-page hero mockup with a serif headline about knowing which draw plan works before you build, a right-side feasibility card showing working-capital limit, draw policy limit, milestone timeline, and 'review starts in minutes' cues, layered over blueprint and Canadian construction imagery. Include subtle license/company proof and a strong coral CTA.
families.focus: Financial feasibility and borrower working-capital relief.
families.decision: Does a capital-planning promise differentiate FairLend from generic construction financing pages?
constraints: do not show exact rates or unverified approvals
keep the feasibility visuals clean and high-level
use premium brokerage styling
families.avoid: fake calculator math, dense spreadsheet UI, hard-sell lending copy, collage, generic banking stock imagery

families.title: Permit To Payout Path
families.summary: Show the journey from proposal, permits, budget, milestones, evidence, approval, to reimbursement payout.
families.businessGoal: Make the seven-step review feel like a governed financing path, not just a lead form.
families.scene: A clean FairLend hero mockup where the main visual is a horizontal path from permit document to budget to milestone to evidence to admin approval to draw release, integrated over a Canadian multiplex blueprint and photo blend. The left headline uses the FairLend serif tone, with chips for no credit check, no documents required, and two minutes, plus a coral project review CTA and small brokerage proof.
families.focus: Process clarity from intake to reimbursement draw release.
families.decision: Will prospects trust the conversion flow more when the hero shows what happens after the form starts?
constraints: do not make a diagram-only page; it should still feel like a premium landing hero
show reimbursement draw release only after completion/approval
text must be sparse
families.avoid: infographic poster, flowchart collage, fake approval guarantees, cramped icon rows

families.title: Brokerage Card As Conversion Anchor
families.summary: Promote the license/proof card into the anchor beside the CTA, turning trust into the reason to start the review now.
families.businessGoal: Use the first page's strongest trust artifact to reduce anxiety around the second page's lead-capture flow.
families.scene: A refined FairLend desktop hero mockup with a large left conversion headline, Step 1 of 7 pill, chips, and stacked CTAs. The dominant right-side visual is a beautiful license/business proof card integrated with a realistic Canadian build-financing scene behind it: blueprint overlay, multifamily property, and a small draw roadmap strip.
families.decision: Does a more prominent license proof card improve the credibility of the project-review CTA?
constraints: the license card should feel official but not like a fake government seal
avoid overloading the hero with legal text
preserve FairLend premium palette
families.avoid: fake seals, fake awards, collage, generic certificate graphic, unreadable legal microcopy
